title: Random Boolean hidden shift

problem.name: Random Boolean hidden shift
problem.statement_latex: For a uniformly random known function $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\{0,1\}$, receive oracle access to $g(x)=f(x+s)$ and identify the uniformly random shift $s$. The known-function description may be used freely in query complexity.
problem.statement_text: For a uniformly random known function $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\{0,1\}$, receive oracle access to $g(x)=f(x+s)$ and identify the uniformly random shift $s$. The known-function description may be used freely in query complexity.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial improvement in the stated resource and parameter regime.
strength.description_text: Polynomial improvement in the stated resource and parameter regime.

evidence.description_latex: The cited results establish a classical lower bound separating the stated quantum resource bound in the specified model.

hardware.description_latex: The query-optimal measurement can require exponentially large preprocessing or circuits for a generic supplied truth table.
hardware.description_text: The query-optimal measurement can require exponentially large preprocessing or circuits for a generic supplied truth table.

quantum.headline_latex: Two queries achieve success tending to one by the Childs--Kothari--Ozols--Rotteler pretty-good measurement. Implementing that measurement can require large circuits for an arbitrary $f$.
quantum.headline_text: Two queries achieve success tending to one by the Childs–Kothari–Ozols–Rotteler pretty-good measurement. Implementing that measurement can require large circuits for an arbitrary $f$.

classical.headline_latex: $\Theta(n)$ one-bit oracle evaluations identify the shift with high probability when unlimited classical computation over the known truth table is free.
